In summary, in spite of being qualitative, this analysis has shown reliably that significant line broadening is observed at projected distances from the star below $\sim$4 au and is absent above.

Evidence for the apparent normality of the wind launching mechanism has been obtained from the presence of large velocities within $\sim$4 au from the centre of the star, the line width increasing from $\sim$5 km s$^{-1}$ FWHM beyond this distance to $\sim$20 km s$^{-1}$ near the star.

At larger distances, up to some 200 au from the centre of the star, the wind morpho-kinematics is dominated by a disc, or equatorial enhancement, expanding isotropically and radially with a velocity not exceeding some 5 km s$^{-1}$, inclined in the north-west/south-east direction with respect to the plane of the sky.
Such morphology is at strong variance with the expectation of a pair of back-to-back outflows collimated by the central gas-and-dust disc.

At larger distances from the star, however, the wind takes the form of expanding discs that are completely unrelated to the morphology of the central gas and dust disc expected to act as a collimator. This suggests that the gas and dust disc did not exist in its present form before the 1994 dimming event.
